name: A job is a record with a journal
summary: A job's life is journalled - submitted, claimed with a lease, heartbeats, steps done, finished, parked - and the journal is the only truth; nothing is inferred from a missing file. Built 2026-11-12 in oco-agent/core: what may follow what in a job's journal is one function, so a finished, expired or parked job cannot be claimed - run once by construction.
why: On 2026-11-11 'pending' was inferred from a missing result, and 102 finished jobs ran again.

name: A voice of its own
summary: The agent's heartbeat is watched from outside the machine, and the client can raise an alarm without the agent.
why: On 2026-11-11 every alert and every message went through the agent that had stalled.

name: Coordination for any driver
summary: ocoeco is the memory and the language of the work; oco-agent is how work is coordinated: it takes work, does it, journals it, and talks with whoever drives it - people and machines alike, each through what suits them (a terminal interface for people, the phone, the command line for machines). It reads and writes ocoeco's shared tables instead of keeping a parallel set, and depends on ocoeco, never the reverse.
why: The author, 2026-11-11: lab-agent and its internals beg to join ocoeco. A whole session wrote every task twice - to the board and to the backlog - and the board's sentences, the inbox and the waits stayed outside the language everything else speaks.

name: Jobs that do not conflict run side by side
summary: A job declares the resources it holds - the phone, a repository, the build machine; jobs that share none run in parallel, so work goes on while a phone reboots or a kernel builds.
why: Waiting is shrunk best by not waiting at all.

name: Resume, never replay
summary: Work is a flow of idempotent steps, each journalled when done; after any interruption the flow resumes at its next step, and a finished job never starts again.
why: A reboot or a reconnect must never be a special case; durable execution and crash-only design show how.

name: The driver's lease
summary: The session driving the lab holds a lease renewed by heartbeats its client sends while it works; when the lease runs out, the agent starts nothing new, parks running work at its next step, and waits to be told to resume.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: if lab-agent has no beat from its driver, it should stop and postpone whatever it is doing.

name: Waits are measured where they happen
summary: Every submit --wait and every wait records itself: what was waited on (a build, a reboot, CI, a harvest), for which project, how long. Gathered into each project's data like commits - made by the work, never typed.
why: The author: waiting is a chore of its own, and grows as more is automated; it must be seen to be shrunk.
